SHELLOPTS is inherited from this harness's invoking shell into every bash subprocess, including errexit, even when a script's own header declares only 'set -uo pipefail' (no -e). A new test case assigning a potentially-failing command substitution directly (var="$(cmd)") silently killed the whole test script mid-run with no visible error, mimicking a crash rather than a reported FAIL. Diagnosed via bash -x tracing; fixed by wrapping the assignment in set +e / set -e 2>/dev/null || true, matching the existing defensive convention already used elsewhere in the same test file. Recorded so a future test-authoring pass does not re-debug the same symptom.

git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check has a double-slash bug: when a file_scope entry already ends in a trailing '/' (e.g. 'agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/'), the containment case pattern builds '${entry}/*' which becomes '...tests//*' (double slash) and fails to match a real touched path like '...tests/test-X.sh' (single slash). This silently dropped 47 of 48 Phase-7-migrated test files from the phase-closing commit (only test-lint-corpus-scan-lib.sh survived, because it also happens to be listed as an exact individual file_scope entry). Separately, lib/common.sh was never committed either because it was omitted from the progress file's files_touched (an authoring gap in this dispatch's own progress-file construction, not the wrapper's fault). Recovered via a follow-up git-commit-scoped.sh commit naming the exact 48 dropped paths explicitly, per the sanctioned FOLLOW-UP-commit recovery pattern for an incomplete phase commit -- not a widened pathspec. Did not fix git-commit-phase.sh itself: it is shared infrastructure outside this task's own file_scope/chartered work.
